title: Molecular shapes
log: 2026-11-01T08:04:32Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The bank card covers linear, bent and tetrahedral shapes but has no pyramidal shape, which the new point requires, and it is broader because it also teaches polarity, so it is not a close enough match to reuse or adapt.

draft.title: Molecular shapes
card: Electron pairs around a central atom repel each other. They move as far apart as possible, and this sets the shape of the molecule.
Count the bonding pairs and lone pairs around the central atom. Each double or triple bond counts as one region, in the same way as a single bond.
two regions, such as CO2, which has two double bonds. The atoms lie in a straight line.

With four regions the pairs point to the corners of a tetrahedron. Four bonds make a tetrahedral shape, as in CH4. Three bonds and one lone pair make pyramidal, as in NH3. Two bonds and two lone pairs make bent, as in H2O. The shape names only the atoms, not the lone pairs.
draft.remember: Count the regions of electrons around the central atom, then name the shape by where the atoms sit.

a.q: Why is a water molecule bent and not linear?
opts: Two lone pairs on oxygen repel the bonding pairs
The two hydrogen atoms repel each other strongly
Oxygen has no lone pairs, so the bonds bend
Hydrogen atoms are smaller than oxygen atoms
a.why: Oxygen has four regions of electrons: two bonding pairs and two lone pairs. They spread out in a tetrahedral arrangement, so the two H atoms sit at an angle. The idea that the hydrogens repel each other is tempting, but the pairs of electrons cause the shape.
a.clue: Look at all the electron pairs on oxygen, not only the bonds.

b.q: Phosphine, PH3, has three P-H bonds and one lone pair on phosphorus. What is its shape?
b.why: There are four regions of electrons, so they point to the corners of a tetrahedron. Only three of them hold atoms, so the atoms form a pyramidal shape. Tetrahedral is tempting, but that needs four bonded atoms.
b.clue: The shape is named by the atoms only, not the lone pair.

a.best: Two lone pairs on oxygen repel the bonding pairs
